name: resource-64mib-stream
title: 64-segment resource stream
summary: Stream 64 maximum-efficient resource segments with compression disabled.
notes: Both implementations carry the same 67,108,800-byte payload in 64 maximum-efficient protocol segments. This is 64 bytes below 64 MiB and avoids making benchmark completion depend on RNS {reference_version}'s timing-sensitive handoff to a 65th 64-byte tail segment.

cell_notes.text: RNS prepares the next 1 MiB segment in a background thread. Prns proves the current segment before that preparation completes, making RNS enter a coarse 50 ms polling loop. A slower stock receiver gives preparation enough time to finish, avoiding that cliff.

description: A single large resource transferred whole, over and over, for a fixed wall-time - the multi-segment bulk mechanism. Each logical transfer is exactly 64 maximum-efficient segments, sent one at a time, hash-proved, and application-acknowledged before another logical transfer begins. The payload repeats one shared deterministic maximum-size block, allowing Prns to stream with bounded memory while both participants transmit identical bytes. Compression is disabled on both stacks.
conformance: Every sent stream settles, receives its ordered application acknowledgement, and is received with exact application-byte totals and zero failures; each transfer is a sequence of hash-proved segments assembled by original_hash before the whole is counted.
